lessons.title: 1. Add a customer
lessons.scenario: A shop, Training Retail {{tag}}, wants to buy from you. Add it as a company customer.
lessons.why: A customer record holds the partner's details once; quotations, deliveries and invoices all point to it.

steps.text: This customer is a company, not an individual.

lessons.explain: Why is the shop set up as a company rather than an individual, and what does that change later?

lessons.title: 2. Add a product
lessons.scenario: You sell Training Widgets for 150 each. Add the product so it can be quoted.
lessons.why: A product carries its sales price and how it is tracked, so every order line starts from the same facts.
lessons.explain: Where will the 150 you entered appear next, and what happens if a quotation needs a different price?

lessons.title: 3. Quote and confirm an order
lessons.scenario: Training Retail {{tag}} orders 2 widgets at the list price. Prepare the quotation, then confirm it as a sales order.
lessons.why: A quotation becomes a sales order when the customer agrees; confirming it is the commitment that triggers delivery and invoicing.

steps.text: Add 2 widgets at the list price.

lessons.explain: What changed when you confirmed the quotation, and what can happen next because of it?
